title: Permissions for Onboarding SaaS Apps for SSPM

blocks.text: You can onboard Software as a Service (SaaS) applications for the SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) scan with read-only permissions. SSPM typically requires read-only access to perform posture assessments.
The following tables list the permissions required for SaaS apps:

blocks.item: A System Administrator User is required to onboard Salesforce for SSPM.

table: Why do we need the permissions?
Permission Sets > App Permissions: Query All Files
User with License: Salesforce/Salesforce API Integration Profile: System Administrator/Minimum Access - API Only Integrations
To execute SOQL to fetch Salesforce organization metadata
Permission Sets > App Permissions: Query All Files Permission Sets > System Permissions: View Health Check Manage Sharing Manage Certificates
User with License: Salesforce/Salesforce API Integration Profile: System Administrator/Minimum Access - API Only Integrations

To read organization settings and metadata Manage Sharing, Manage Certificates are not read only and inevitable since Salesforce does not have any granular permission related to them due to the permission model of Salesforce.
Permission Sets > System Permissions: Modify Metadata through Metadata API Functions Customize Application
User with License: Salesforce/Salesforce API Integration Profile: System Administrator/Minimum Access - API Only Integrations
To fetch and remedy Salesforce metadata like remote site settings, connected apps, etc. This permission is inevitable since there is no read-only equivalent permission to access metadata API.
Permission Sets > System Permissions: Modify All Data
User with License: Salesforce/Salesforce API Integration Profile: System Administrator/Minimum Access - API Only Integrations

blocks.item: An Integration System User is required to onboard Workday for SSPM.

table: Why do we need the permissions?
To execute the SELECT query via the WQL endpoint to retrieve account metadata
To view account-level security settings, including accountDisabledOrExpired, sessionTimeoutMinutes, and isIntegrationUser
To read security policies, MFA settings (one_TimePasscode...), and authentication exclusions
To provide read access to system logs and audit trails, specifically for the timeOfMostRecentSignOn field
To provide access to basic identity fields like username and emailAddress for reporting
To view data-retention flags and determine if an account is marked for deletion (isEligibleForPurge)
To view current job profiles and employment status to verify if accounts belong to active workers
To provide general read access to worker profiles and business processes related to staffing
(Broad Category) To cover core worker identity and employment status links
(Broad Category) To enable technical data retrieval and access to the WQL engine
To provide view-only access to audit Integration System Users and their specific flags
To read organizational hierarchies to contextualize account permissions and role assignments
